summary: Verified the Platform Owner login bug fix end-to-end. Backend: 6 new login-bug tests + 13 iter-6 regressions + 24 platform-owner regressions = 43/43 PASSED (serial, -n 0). Frontend Playwright: fresh login as maher@tapbyned.com redirects to Dashboard, sidebar+footer render user, Platform Admin link present, impersonation-banner absent (count=0). Stale ned_token_original='stale' + ned_token='old-invalid' set in localStorage before login are BOTH cleared after login, and no banner appears. Logout clears both ned_token and ned_token_original and navigates to /auth/login. Backend edge cases verified: whitespace email stripped, case-insensitive email login, wrong password still 401, empty password rejected. Password unchanged (still NedTechOwner2026!).
critical_code_review_comments: test_platform_owner.py::TestSeed::test_idempotent_on_restart restarts supervisor:backend which causes 502s in parallel test workers (pytest.ini uses xdist -n 2 --dist loadscope). Recommend marking this test @pytest.mark.serial or running xdist with --dist loadfile and pinning restarts to a single worker. All tests pass with -n 0.
authContext.jsx: fetchMe() catches ANY error and removes ned_token — including transient 5xx/network blips. Consider narrowing to 401 to avoid silent forced-logout on backend hiccups.

apiClient.js 401 interceptor navigates via window.location.href — full reload wipes React state; that is fine here but combined with fetchMe() removing token on any error means a single failed /auth/me can loop. Consider skipping interceptor redirect for /auth/me path.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend tests serially: `pytest backend/tests/ -n 0`. Running in parallel fails because test_idempotent_on_restart restarts the backend and races other workers with 502s. Login bug is fully fixed on both backend (whitespace/case handling) and frontend (stale ned_token_original cleanup in login/register/logout and 401 interceptor; ImpersonationBanner reads JWT claim only).
rca of the issue: Reproduction: 1) Log in as platform_owner, 2) Perform impersonation which sets ned_token_original in localStorage, 3) Log out (previous logout removed only ned_token, leaving ned_token_original), 4) Log back in — ImpersonationBanner previously derived isImpersonating from localStorage.getItem('ned_token_original'), so it rendered permanently, making the user believe login failed. Mitigation now in place: (a) authContext login/register/logout all removeItem('ned_token_original'); (b) apiClient 401 interceptor also purges it; (c) ImpersonationBanner only trusts JWT user.impersonating_from; (d) backend /auth/login strips+lowers email so pasted trailing spaces and capitalization no longer cause invalid-credentials 401. All verified passing.
